newsitem.title: USA: Mass gov plans new convention center for Boston.
newsitem.headline: Mass gov plans new convention center for Boston.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov William Weld on Wednesday said he proposed a bill for a new, $695 million convention center in South Boston, which would be paid for by raising hotel taxes and selling revenue bonds.

The plan calls for the city to spend up to $125 million to buy the site on Summer Street, while the state would sell up to $575 million of revenue bonds, said Joe Landolfi, a spokesman for the executive office for Administration and Finance.

The bill was based largely on a report done in March by consultants for a working group that was charged with brokering the final plan for the facility, which will augment the Hynes Convention Center and house a 600,000 square foot main exhibit hall with 235,000 square feet of additional meeting space.

The working group included representatives picked by Senate President Thomas Birmingham, House Speaker Thomas Finneran, Mayor Thomas Menino and Weld. Because all these officials had a chance to influence the plan, Landolfi hoped the bill, which he called a priority, would soon be approved. "We think we've really narrowed the canvas in terms of differences," he said.
The bill also provides state support for a convention center in Worcester, the Basketball Hall of Fame in Springfield, the National Music Center in Lenox, and the Kerr Mill Development in Fall River.

Weld predicted the new center would create over 6,000 new, direct jobs and 4,000 "indirect and induced" jobs through-out the state. The number of jobs needed to build the center was estimated at over 3,500.

The bonds for the new center, which the Republican governor said Boston needed to compete for large convention and trade shows, would be supported by about $43 million of revenue a year. The proposed revenue stream includes increasing the hotel room occupancy tax to 12 percent from 9.7 percent, provided voters in Cambridge and Boston approve the rise in referenda.
